- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +2% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., > 0.30) and price is trending up, model underestimates continuation — add 2–5% to forecast mean.
- Model frequently overestimates short-term volatility — smooth 30d forecast by averaging last 7–10 days’ values before final output.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., +0.30+ in 2+ days), model lags — delay forecast rise by 1–2 days or adjust downward by 1–3%.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.20), model tends to overpredict — apply 3–5% downward bias to forecast mean.
- Model often fails to capture sentiment-driven mean reversion — if sentiment is negative for 5+ days, force forecast to revert to 10–15 day moving average.
